question.problem: Victoria has the $4$ playing cards: the ace of clubs, the ace of diamonds, the ace of hearts, and the ace of spades. She takes one card and places it in front of her. She then does the same with another card. In how many different ways can she choose a sequence of $2$ cards like this?
question.worked_solution:
The number of permutations of $n$ objects taken $r$ at a time is given by the formula

$$
{}_{n}{P}_{r}=\frac{n!}{(n-r)!}.
$$

There are $4$ cards, so $n=4.$ We want to select $2$ of those cards to make a sequence of $2$ cards, so we have $r=2.$ 

Therefore, the number of different ways to choose the cards is 

$$
\begin{aligned}{}_{4}{P}_{2} & =\frac{4!}{(4-2)!} \\  & =\frac{4!}{2!} \\  & =\frac{4\cdot 3\cdot \cancel{2!}}{\cancel{2!}} \\  & =4\cdot 3 \\  & =12.\end{aligned}
$$
